clue.text: Sweet acting family not without love

parts.note: the Fondas (Henry, Jane, Peter, Bridget) are a famous Hollywood acting family

indicators.note: without tells us to remove a letter from the word not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A dynasty of actors is described as cold and loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like a description of the family, but it is the definition, a noun for a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft creamy confection, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Learner in wonderful times hanging loose?

indicators.note: in sets the learner's letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: fab is slang for wonderful
L is the learner sign on a car
by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A student having a marvellous time is just hanging about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging loose' sounds like relaxing; here it describes sagging flesh, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby flesh is soft and slack, so it droops or sags rather than being firm.

clue.text: Swedish neighbour impossible, keeping rook

indicators.note: keeping means holding the rook letter inside

parts.note: no way is an exclamation meaning impossible
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A Swede declares it impossible that the neighbour keeps a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook is a bird, but here it is the chess piece, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway shares a long land border with Sweden, so it is that country's neighbour.

clue.text: Party sheltered in turbulent rain, bane of Scottish city

indicators.note: sheltered in means the party word is enclosed by the other letters
turbulent suggests churning the letters of rain and bane

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party took cover from stormy rain, the curse of a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges RAIN and BANE into ABERNIAN, and 'sheltered in' puts the party inside that; Aberdeen is notoriously rainy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdonian describes something or someone from Aberdeen, the city in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Edison contemporary creates lakeside houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rival inventor of Edison's builds lakeside homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was an inventor working at the same time as Thomas Edison, his famous rival.

clue.text: Old canine trained — beginning to talk?

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters of canine being drilled into a new order
beginning to points at only the opening letter of talk

parts.note: first letter of talk

explanation.surface: An elderly dog, having been trained, is on the point of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges CANINE into ANCIEN, and 'beginning to talk' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is a straightforward synonym of old, meaning belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: Sign in gold to put on chart

indicators.note: put on means the earlier pieces sit on top of chart in this down entry

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: Instructions for signing a chart in gold ink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'put on' places AU and TO above GRAPH.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a signature, and to autograph is to sign something.

clue.text: Fish, grouse or beef

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to grouse is to complain
third meaning: to beef is also to complain

explanation.walkthrough: Grouse is a game bird and beef a meat, making a menu, but both are verbs for moaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a freshwater fish and also a verb for complaining or nagging.

clue.text: Look in skip — for thin veal slice?

indicators.note: in puts the word for look inside the word for skip

parts.note: to skip is to escape, as in skipping town
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a rubbish skip hunting for a cutlet.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British builder's rubbish container, but here it is a verb meaning to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, classically veal, beaten flat.

clue.text: Magnanimous English group backing rave

indicators.note: backing means the English and group letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: A generous English band supports a rave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns English plus group round to give TOLE, before the rave word.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnanimous person is generous and forgiving, readily putting up with others.

clue.text: Fit silver on table at last

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
RE means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: at last points at the final letter of table

parts.note: last letter of table

explanation.surface: Silverware has been arranged suitably on the dining table at last.
explanation.walkthrough: AG, then RE (on, as in 'regarding'), then E from the end of 'table'.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree with something is to match or suit it, as when one thing fits another.

clue.text: Like Private Eye, demolishing racialist

indicators.note: demolishing knocks the word racialist down so its letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A magazine's attack demolishes a racist.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a long-running British magazine of political mockery and lampoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye is famous for mocking public figures, so it is a satirical publication.

clue.text: Year in company great on the whole

indicators.note: in places the letter for year inside the word for company

parts.note: a band is a company or group of people
large means great in size

explanation.surface: A year spent in a firm is described as great overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a business, but it is a group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning generally or overall, the same as on the whole.

clue.text: Obscure combo that rivalled Oasis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to obscure is to make indistinct
second meaning: ... were the Britpop band who rivalled Oasis in the 1990s

explanation.walkthrough: A combo is a band; Blur and Oasis fought the 'Battle of Britpop' chart war in 1995.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make something hazy, and the noun names a famous British rock group.

clue.text: In Hull, city racecourse for chariots

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip
a hull is the outer husk of a seed, a pod
Rome is a city

explanation.surface: A venue in the English city of Hull hosts chariot racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is the husk of a pea, POD.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a hippodrome was the arena where horse and chariot races were held.

clue.text: Personality from Poplar, in age fantastic, newsreader initially

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters being wildly transformed into a new order
initially picks out the opening letter of newsreader

parts.note: first letter of newsreader

explanation.surface: A celebrity hailing from the London district of Poplar, still fabulous in old age, was a newsreader.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Rippon is a British TV presenter who was one of the BBC's first female newsreaders. Rearrange POPLAR, IN, AGE plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a well-known television figure, so she counts as a media personality or celebrity.

clue.text: Vessel recently located, complete, united leaderless country

parts.note: to end something is to complete it

indicators.note: leaderless means the country loses its first letter

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A ship has been found, finishing off a united nation without a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Shackleton's ship Endurance sank in Antarctica in 1915 and its wreck was found in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackleton's polar ship, lost in Antarctic ice, had its wreck found in 2022.

clue.text: Does this suggest I step on virgin snow?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: PISTE knocked off, i.e. jumbled, gives these two words

explanation.surface: A skier wonders whether to tread on fresh untouched snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Take 'off' as an anagram signal working on PISTE: the result is I STEP, so the clue asks for the phrase that would produce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing off-piste means away from groomed runs, on fresh untracked powder.

clue.text: I'm in European country for evaluation

indicators.note: in puts I'm inside the other letters

parts.note: a state is a country
I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A speaker announces they are in a European nation for an assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is a rough calculation or judgement of value, i.e. an assessment.

clue.text: Fine spinach dish replaced traditional meal

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

indicators.note: replaced says these letters are put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A tasty spinach dish has supplanted a classic dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips is the classic British takeaway: battered fish with thick-cut fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered fish with fried potatoes is the iconic British takeaway, a long-established national dinner.

clue.text: Imagine not starting cryptic puzzle!

indicators.note: cryptic suggests the remaining letters are disguised by reordering
not starting means the word Imagine drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A solver is told not to start imagining a cryptic puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic puzzle' reads as one phrase, but 'cryptic' is the anagram signal working on MAGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling to work out.

clue.text: Fellow traveller elevated — it's the booze

indicators.note: elevated means read upwards in this down entry, so backwards

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A fellow traveller is high, blaming the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow traveller' looks like one phrase, a political sympathiser, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: One cutting into roast creates bother

indicators.note: cutting into puts the letter for one inside the word for roast

parts.note: to pan or roast someone is to criticise them harshly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone carving a joint of roast meat finds it troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' looks culinary, but it means to criticise, PAN; I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain is a nuisance or an annoyance, the same idea as a bother.

clue.text: Papers taken into French region's capital

indicators.note: taken into places the letters for papers inside the region's name

parts.note: Provence is a region of south-eastern France
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents have been brought into a French province's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to belong to Provence, but it is the definition: Providence is the capital of Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the state capital of Rhode Island in the United States.

clue.text: Monkey minus tail in animation

indicators.note: minus tail means the monkey word loses its final letter

parts.note: the vervet is an African monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey that has lost its tail appears in a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animation' suggests cartoons but means liveliness here.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is energy and enthusiasm, the same as liveliness or animation.

clue.text: Partner's surgery evidently reversible?

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

indicators.note: evidently reversible says the surgery word appears again turned round, so the whole reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A spouse's operation can apparently be undone.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is British slang for a colleague or partner; OP followed by its reversal gives a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is informal British slang for a mate, colleague or opposite number.

clue.text: Generous sort welcoming writer in Whetstone?

indicators.note: welcoming means the outer word takes the writer in

parts.note: a sharer is a generous person who shares
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person hosts an author in Whetstone, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Whetstone is a London suburb, but here it is the stone used to hone blades; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone is one kind of sharpener, a stone used to put an edge on knives.

clue.text: Heart, perhaps, that may be stopped in church?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the heart is an example of a bodily ...

definitions.text: that may be stopped in church?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a church ... has stops, knobs that select its pipes

explanation.walkthrough: Stopping a heart sounds fatal, but organ stops are the controls on a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a body part such as the heart and the keyboard instrument with stops played in church.

clue.text: Hideous sight I witnessed in the auditorium?

indicators.note: in the auditorium means what an audience would hear rather than read

parts.note: I witnessed is I saw

explanation.surface: Someone recounts seeing something ugly at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, 'I saw' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, an unsightly thing.

clue.text: Eastern male, messenger casting first stone

indicators.note: casting first means throwing off the opening letter of the messenger word

parts.note: a herald is a messenger

explanation.surface: An Eastern man carrying a message throws the first stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting first stone' evokes the biblical phrase, but 'casting first' drops the H from HERALD, and 'stone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green gemstone, and a precious gem is commonly called a stone.
